tool_order: After actual release/deployment and a fresh /version read, invoke fixed-query collector with --samples 5 --require-server-timing to a new output
Then capture all 206 static-source/evidence files and sixteen recovery windows with fresh version/footer fences
If no natural scan or the first capture is incomplete, retain it and permit at most one later identical capture after normal cache lifecycle; never purge or vary parameters
comparison_requirements: Each individual capture has equal before/after version fences and valid server timings
Retain every request, HTTP refusal/failure, missing header, cache path and actual elapsed time
Match query, encoding, total/row counts and decoded response-byte hashes for before/after interpretation; a mismatch requires semantic/currentness review
Never compare ranking/page_hit/waited_hit to scan as an optimization effect
Client latency includes TLS/network/decode; server total includes child stages, which are never added again
Scope may include SQL; stage times alone do not establish a PostgreSQL query plan or pure CPU cost
Missing natural scan remains unavailable; release or first-request ordering does not prove cold database/cache
diagnostic_goal: Identify whether naturally observed scan time is dominated by scan_fetch, scope, selection, serialization or lock_wait before promoting the Tc selection experiment
single_scan_scope: A diagnostic observation, not p95, statistical significance or production performance acceptance
